title.narrative: Second Upper Secondary Education Sector Development Program

description.narrative: The proposed Second Upper Secondary Education Sector Development Program (USESDP 2) is part of the phased support of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to develop high-quality human resources by improving the effectiveness of upper secondary education (USE). It builds on and complements ADB's ongoing Upper Secondary Education Sector Development Program (USESDP 1). The program will (i) improve teacher quality and boost the quality and labor market relevance of USE; and (ii) strengthen institutional capacity for USE planning, management, and delivery. While the policy reforms will apply nationwide, the project activities will cover only selected areas.

Reports and Recommendations of the President
Loan 3719: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 03 Jun 2025
Loan 3720: 95% of contracts awarded and 94% disbursed as of 03 Jun 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: Program: The Royal Government of Cambodia complied with the required policy actions stipulated for the release of the policy-based loan, and accordingly, ADB released $15 million in March 2019 to support USE reform implementation.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jun 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/47136/47136-006-apfs-en_3.pdf
Some results are in the Environmental and Social Monitoring Reports | Jun 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/47136/47136-006-esmr-en_5.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1: Key achievements by Q2 2021 include: finalized draft of the new organizational structure of the National Institute of Education (NIE); completed review of the NIE five-year strategic plan 20192023 and prepared the first draft of the NIE 10-year strategic plan; and finalized the NIE human resources manual.While the firm to prepare the masterplan for the NIE Campus renovation, upgrading and redevelopment has been contracted since October 2020, the international specialists have not been able to travel to Cambodia because of the COVID-19 travel restrictions which also led to the delay in the preparation of the masterplan. Regular virtual meetings were instead conducted with the masterplan consultants to discuss plans and concepts. On the other hand, the consulting firm to handle design and construction supervision of the NIE campus renovation was mobilized in August 2021.Technical specifications of ICT (hardware and software) equipment (including for videoconferencing) for NIE teachers have been completed. The laptops for NIE teachers' training stations have been procured and delivered to the NIE in January 2021.Two NIE lecturers have been selected as scholars to pursue their master's degree in library management, while 5 candidates were selected for the PhD programs in science (physics, chemistry, biology), computer science, management education and curriculum-teaching methods. On the other hand, the training of upper secondary STEM teachers from 50 Secondary Resource Schools (SRSs) and 81 upper secondary school network schools and 40 NIE STEM lecturers on the new curriculum framework, content knowledge, instruction, and assessment had to be postponed to Q2 2022 in view of the COVID-19 safety restrictions.The pre-service training (PRESET) and in-service training (INSET) programs, syllabi and materials for upper secondary school teachers, inspectors, and school directors have been developed, reviewed and endorsed by MoEYS. School-based Management (SBM) training materials and manuals have been selected and Inspection training materials prepared. KAPE and VSO have finalized the STEM and Library training materials and manuals for the professional development program for NIE librarians. Output 2:A draft Operations Manual for Career Education with local industry partnerships has been finalized and translated into Khmer. Training participants from the target schools have already been identified.Procurement activities for the renovation of classrooms into science rooms, upgrading of ICT rooms, and conversion of classrooms into multipurpose, project-based life skills classrooms as well as the equipment and resources for the renovated classrooms and science labs is ongoing. Three works packages with total cost estimate of US$5.2 million were advertised and the bid evaluation reports are currently being prepared. Two multiple-lot goods/equipment packages with total cost estimate of US$1.18 million were partially awarded and are being rebidded due to lack of responsive bids. The contracts for these packages are expected to be awarded in Q4 2021. The 20 SRSs, and 30 SRS USS network schools to be provided with solar panels have been identified. The bill of quantities (BOQs), specifications and costings are currently being prepared for submission to the EA's Procurement Department in September 2021. Other works and goods packages are in the initial stages of the procurement process, i.e., preparation of BOQs, technical specifications, and gathering of inputs from the project/component units and consultants. Advertisement of these packages is expected to commence in Q4 2021.Output 3:The training materials, program, and targets on the new Regional Inspection system for directors from the 25 provincial and municipal departments of education, and the directors of the 150 resource schools on inspection have been finalized. Training is being planned in Q2 2022. On the other hand, the SBM training materials, programs, committees, and budget plan for the 50 SRS schools are being finalized and/or updated. The Directorate General of Education, with VSO, are updating the tools for SRS monitoring, mentoring and coaching, which will be the basis of the subsequent training scheduled in Q1 2022. The International Specialists tasked to conduct the training on examination design were unable to travel to Cambodia due to COVID-19 related travel restrictions. In the interim, the specialists are supporting the drafting of a report on the student assessment system and developing guidelines for development of and implementation of the assessment criteria.MOEYS has developed research questionnaires on teacher needs and supply in 50 SRSs which will be analyzed and used to inform the teacher deployment policy reform to be developed and implemented.The Department of Information Technology (DIT) conducted workshops on experimental video production for grade 10 mathematics and chemistry with several participants; produced and posted videos on USE STEM subjects; and continued to create content and storyboards for video production on grade 11 STEM subjects.
